## Citation statement
Please cite these materials as: Waterfield, E., Ihle, M., Schönbrodt, F., & Von Grebmer zu Wolfsthurn, S. (2026). *Introduction to literate programming with Quarto* [Quarto slides]. [LMU Open Science Center](https://www.osc.lmu.de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-tools/quarto](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-tools/quarto)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to **introduce Quarto**, an open-source publishing system that allows users to **combine text, code, and other outputs** to create **reproducible reports**, **presentations**, and **websites**. Learners will experience the basic **workflow of creating and editing Quarto documents**, **rendering** them into different formats, and using Quarto within an R-based research workflow. Learners will focus on practicing different Quarto elements to structure documents, include analysis results, and control the appearance of their outputs. In addition, the session demonstrates **how to add citations** and automatically generate a bibliography using Zotero. Through this guided, hands-on tutorial, learners will **create their own Quarto document**, render it into a finished output, and learn how to **publish and share** their work online using **GitHub Pages**. 

### Who are these materials for?

- **Educators** in higher education with or without familiarity with open research planning to **teach open research novices**
- **Self-learners** with no or limited familiarity with open research planning to **develop and build** up on their open research skills

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;"> 
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| R and RStudio installed | Latest versions of both R and RStudio | [Download RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) |
| Basic R skills | Introduction to R - Part I | [Access here]() |
| Advanced R skills | Introduction to R - Part II | [Access here]() |
| Basic Git skills | Introduction to version control with Git in RStudio | [Access here]() |
| Collaborating on GitHub | Introduction to collaborative coding with GitHub |  [Access here]() |
| Zotero | Reference Management Tool | [Download Link](https://www.zotero.org/) |
</div>


### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you or your learners will be able to ...

- **Create**, **edit**, and **render** Quarto documents
- **Use key Quarto features** like code chunks, YAML headers, citations, and output formatting
- **Insert citations** and **generate a bibliography** with Zotero directly into the Quarto document
- **Publish** and **share** your work using GitHub Pages
